periods.analysis: Yellow at 26 days/yr rolling, against a target of <=20 and with no prior quarter in this run to compare. That is not a failure, but it is too close to the yellow ceiling of 28 for a city with an airport, seaport, and low-lying freight routes to treat as background noise. The worst repeat locations were Bayfront Avenue at Outfall OF-22, the Seaport Gate 3 approach, and the northbound Airport Connector sump near PS-SD-04. The pipes and tide gates are doing what their age says they will do; they are giving us warning before they give us a shutdown.
periods.recommendations: Keep this in yellow management, not routine monitoring. Have the Stormwater West crew complete CCTV on OF-22 and the Mill Canal trunk between MH-4418 and MH-4431 before the November king tide set. Sustain the green portions of the system by continuing monthly exercising of tide gates TG-12 through TG-18 and adding the Airport Connector sump to the preventive-maintenance route.

periods.analysis: Yellow again, now at 28 days/yr rolling, up 2 days from 26 in 2024-Q3 and sitting exactly on the yellow limit. The December king tides and two south-wind rain events put water over the curb at Bayfront and backed up the Seaport Gate 3 trench drain twice. Crews cleared 14 tons of grit and eelgrass from the Harbor Cut and Mill Canal screens, which helped response time but did not change the rolling count. This is the part of the graph where I stop accepting anecdotes and start defending budget with asset condition data.
periods.recommendations: Hold the measure on the weekly department scorecard until it moves back below 26 or has a funded correction plan. Issue the small works package for flap-valve replacements SW-1127, SW-1131, and SW-1134, with completion before the March tide cycle. Extend the useful work already happening by keeping the vacuum truck on the Port Loop route every other Friday through winter, not just after complaints.

periods.analysis: Red at 30 days/yr rolling, up 2 days from 28 in 2024-Q4 and now above the >28 red threshold. The trigger was not one dramatic flood; it was repeat nuisance flooding at the same assets during January tide stacking and February rain on saturated ground. PS-SD-04 ran within 8 percent of firm capacity twice, and TG-17 at Mill Canal showed delayed closure on both inspections. This is concerned-but-managed: the field evidence is clear, and the weak links are named.
periods.recommendations: Move the Mill Canal and Airport Connector stormwater work into the first tranche of Pipeline Renewal, with TG-17, PS-SD-04 controls, and the 54-inch CMP segment MC-54-08 treated as linked work. Authorize design to 60 percent by the end of 2025-Q2, not another study memo. Keep the functioning downtown underdrain program going and extend its catch-basin sensor pilot from 12 to 20 locations so dispatch sees the surge before the phones light up.

periods.analysis: Red at 32 days/yr rolling, up another 2 days from 30 in 2025-Q1. Spring should have given us a little breathing room, so the continued rise tells me this is not just winter weather showing up in the denominator. Public Works crews logged repeat ponding on the Seaport Truck Route near CB-7802 after three ordinary high tides, and the old backflow preventer at OF-22 failed a bench test. The problem remains managed, but the curve is moving the wrong way with enough consistency to justify capital acceleration.
periods.recommendations: Accelerate the Pipeline Renewal bid package for OF-22 and MC-54-08 and split long-lead valves out for early procurement through the on-call vendor, TideWorks Mechanical. Put temporary bladder protection at OF-22 for the July and August tide windows and assign the East Basin crew to inspect it after every tide above 10.8 feet. Sustain system reliability elsewhere by keeping the lower-risk outfalls on quarterly inspection rather than borrowing those hours for emergency work.

periods.analysis: Red at 34 days/yr rolling, up 2 days from 32 in 2025-Q2. Summer usually hides drainage sins, but this quarter added days during two tropical remnants and a high astronomical tide that backed water into the Bayfront laterals. The new telemetry at 18 catch basins confirmed what crews have been saying: the Seaport Gate 3 approach floods first, drains last, and is not being solved by cleaning alone. I do not like a red measure that keeps adding 2 days a quarter, but I do like having enough instrumented proof to stop guessing.
periods.recommendations: Keep Pipeline Renewal focused on the named assets and do not dilute it into a citywide wish list. Approve night work permits for the Seaport Gate 3 trench drain reconstruction so port operations stay open while crews replace the undersized 18-inch run with 30-inch pipe. Extend the catch-basin telemetry pilot to the Bayfront Avenue corridor and sustain weekly debris pulls at Harbor Cut through leaf season.

periods.analysis: Red at 36 days/yr rolling, up 2 days from 34 in 2025-Q3. The fourth straight 2-day increase is the plain fact, and it means the rolling year is still absorbing more flooded days than it is dropping. November king tides tested every weak point we already had on the board: TG-17 lagged, OF-22 overtopped, and the Airport Connector sump needed manual assist on one shift. Crews kept lanes open with pumps and cones, which is good operations, but it is not infrastructure capacity.
periods.recommendations: Lock the Pipeline Renewal construction schedule before year-end, with TG-17 replacement first and OF-22 backflow work second. Put two trailer pumps at PS-SD-04 and one at Seaport Gate 3 under a winter standby contract, with fuel and hose staged rather than ordered during the event. Sustain the routes that are performing by keeping the Central Basin cleaning cycle at 45 days, because stealing from good assets is how they become bad assets.

periods.analysis: Red at 37 days/yr rolling, up 1 day from 36 in 2025-Q4. The increase slowed, which I will take, but 37 is still 17 days over the <=20 target and well above the red threshold of >28. January storms put less water into downtown than last year because the temporary bladders and pump staging worked, but the rolling count still picked up a day on the Airport Connector during a tide-plus-rain overlap. The field story is shifting from uncontrolled deterioration to active containment, and that is better, not good.
periods.recommendations: Keep the containment plan in place until permanent Pipeline Renewal assets are commissioned; do not demobilize the standby pumps just because the slope improved. Require weekly look-ahead meetings among Stormwater, Port operations, and the airport access team through the March tide cycle. Extend the successful temporary bladder setup at OF-22 to Outfall OF-24 for the next king tide, while maintaining normal preventive maintenance on tide gates that are still closing cleanly.

periods.analysis: Red at 38 days/yr rolling, up 1 day from 37 in 2026-Q1. The rate of increase is still slower than the 2-day quarterly jumps we saw through 2025, but the measure is moving the wrong way and remains nearly double the target of <=20. Early Pipeline Renewal work is visible: TG-17 fabrication passed shop inspection, and the MC-54-08 bypass plan was tested on a dry run, but the assets are not yet in the ground. Until they are, the city is still relying on crews, pumps, and tide timing to protect freight movement and neighborhoods.
periods.recommendations: Hold the red status and manage to construction milestones, not optimism. Start TG-17 installation in the first low-tide work window of July and require daily production reports from the contractor until the gate is commissioned. Keep the temporary pump contract active through hurricane season, and sustain the expanded sensor network so we can verify whether the completed Pipeline Renewal work actually bends the rolling days/yr count down.

periods.analysis: Illustrative September import: rolling tidal and storm flooding increased from 38 to 39 days per year, against a target of no more than 20. Gate, bypass, and pumping work has not yet produced a measured reduction.
periods.recommendations: Maintain temporary protection and check installation and commissioning evidence before attributing any future change in flood days to permanent works.
